observed.source: Codex session rollout (CLI-recorded thread settings; not model-authored)

result.decision_rationale: The required unit gate passed on the pushed candidate. The command handles healthy enrollments, missing state files and invalid JSON, but a single claim with a non-string directory can still prevent every enrollment from being listed. The review also found cases where the PR field has the wrong output type, a relative state path depends on the caller’s working directory, and reading a network share violates the local-only requirement.

executed_verification: The CLI-recorded transcript confirms the guarded push of af2d1768c1d775e84c1cb6f68452df9c4c14d707 followed by verification of the unit gate on that commit. The controller recorded exit code 0 and an unchanged worktree.
The gate log shows 194 tests run with one supplemental live smoke skipped. All three ListCommandTests passed. The log’s SHA-256 matches the controller receipt.
inspected: Fixed mission, full feature diff, repository instructions, operating guide, protocol, developer report, tool transcript, gate receipt and log, and empty prior-findings ledger.
Registry claim creation, state path handling, CLI dispatch, real temporary-repository fixtures, new behavior tests, and README command documentation.
limitations: The reviewer used read-only inspection. Executed behavior is attributed to the recorded candidate gate. The four findings follow from source inspection.
required_gaps: Regression coverage for malformed directory values, invalid PR-number types, listing from a different working directory, and refusing network-backed state paths before access.
source_inspection_only: The list branch returns before constructing a controller or acquiring a workflow lock. For ordinary local paths it reads the registry and state files directly.
The existing tests cover a held writer lock, unchanged fixture contents, empty and absent registries, missing state, malformed JSON, and enrollment-ID ordering.

findings.actual: A nonzero number or nonempty object passes the truthiness check. Path(claim["dir"]) then raises TypeError outside the per-claim handler, and the command exits before printing the array. JSON decoding can likewise raise an uncaught RecursionError for an excessively nested file.
findings.blocking_rationale: One damaged entry can hide all healthy enrollments, contrary to the explicit failure-isolation requirement.
findings.expected: The command prints both rows and exits successfully. The damaged row retains its available identity, has status unknown, and explains the error.
findings.requested_correction: Validate that dir is a nonempty string before constructing the path, and handle JSON decoder recursion failures within the affected entry.
findings.requested_evidence: Add fixture cases with a non-string dir and excessively nested JSON alongside a healthy claim. Assert successful exit, an error on each damaged row, and the healthy row’s expected values.
findings.title: A malformed registry entry can abort the entire listing
findings.trigger: List a registry containing a healthy enrollment and a valid JSON claim whose dir value is a nonzero number.

findings.actual: The code checks that pr is an object, then copies its number member verbatim. A stored string or object is emitted directly in the output.
findings.blocking_rationale: Consumers cannot rely on the required number-or-null output type when one state file is damaged.
findings.expected: Every row has a numeric PR number or JSON null.
findings.requested_correction: Validate the stored PR number before adding it to the row. Emit null for an invalid value.
findings.requested_evidence: Add a behavior test with a readable state object whose pr.number is a string. Assert that the row remains present and its pr field is null.
findings.title: A damaged state file can produce an invalid PR field
findings.trigger: List an enrollment whose state.json contains a pr object with a nonnumeric number member.

findings.actual: Enrollment accepts a relative --state-root and stores str(folder) in the claim. The new command interprets that path relative to the directory where list runs. A healthy enrollment can therefore appear missing or show state from a different file.
findings.blocking_rationale: An owner listing the machine-wide registry from another working directory can receive an incorrect enrollment status.
findings.expected: The displayed status comes from the enrollment’s own state directory regardless of where the owner invokes list.
findings.requested_correction: Persist an absolute state directory for new claims created with a relative state root. Handle existing relative claims explicitly when their original location cannot be determined reliably.
findings.requested_evidence: Enroll with a relative state root, change to a different working directory, and assert that list still returns the real enrollment’s fields. Cover the diagnostic for an ambiguous older claim.
findings.title: Relative state roots make the listing depend on the caller’s directory
findings.trigger: Enroll with a relative --state-root, then invoke list from another directory.

findings.actual: The command passes the directory from the claim directly to read_json. On Windows a UNC path causes the filesystem to contact the share. The test’s Python socket and subprocess checks do not observe filesystem-initiated network access.
findings.blocking_rationale: A machine-wide inspection can initiate network I/O or wait on an unavailable share despite the command’s strict no-network contract.
findings.expected: The command returns an unknown row explaining that it cannot inspect remote state under its local-only contract.
findings.requested_correction: Identify network-backed state paths before opening the file and return a per-claim diagnostic while continuing to list local enrollments.
findings.requested_evidence: Add a Windows behavior test with a claim naming a UNC state directory and a healthy local neighbor. Verify the remote-path diagnostic and the healthy row without contacting a live share.
findings.title: Reading a network-backed state directory can initiate network access
findings.trigger: A Windows registry claim names a state directory on a UNC share.

summary.delivered_behavior: For ordinary local claims, list prints a sorted JSON array with the requested fields. The candidate tests confirm that it works while a writer lock is held, prints [] for an empty registry, and retains rows for missing files and invalid JSON. The README documents the command next to status.
remaining_owner_review: Final product acceptance and the decision whether to merge after the blocking findings are resolved and the corrected candidate is reviewed.
summary.scope_reviewed: The complete list-command mission at the final checkpoint, including implementation, behavior tests, documentation, guarded push, and candidate-bound unit verification.
